slides.big: Why so many dads are quietly doing two jobs right now.
slides.small: The more you try to look "too valuable to cut," the faster you burn out.

Since the last round of layoffs, you say yes to everything.
You answer faster. You stay later.
You took on their work without a word.
Your brain thinks: "If I'm the hardest worker here, they can't let me go."

Layoffs come from spreadsheets, not effort.
The top reasons companies give are the economy, restructuring and AI.
Not who stayed latest.

slides.big: So protect yourself the smart way:
slides.small:
1. Keep a running list of your wins.
2. Update your resume quietly. Just in case.
3. Stay close to one person outside your team.
Then go home on time.

slides.big:
Fear makes you work harder.
It doesn't make you safer.
slides.small:

caption:
Why so many dads are quietly doing two jobs right now. 👇

Since the last round of layoffs, you say yes to everything.
You answer faster. You stay later.
You picked up their work without a word.

That's not ambition. That's fear.
Your brain is trying to make you "too valuable to cut."

But layoffs come from spreadsheets, not effort. When companies explain their cuts, the top reasons are the economy, restructuring and AI. Not who stayed the latest.

Why it matters: fear makes you work harder. It doesn't make you safer. It just makes you more tired, and your family gets even less of you.

slides.big: Why the hardest workers keep getting passed over.
slides.small: I thought I needed to work harder. Turns out, I needed people to see the work.

You did the work.
In the meeting, a coworker talks about it like it was his.
The boss nods at him.
You say nothing.

slides.big: It's not that you're not good enough.
slides.small:
Bosses notice what gets said out loud.
Work done quietly is work nobody sees.

slides.big: And here's what it costs you:
slides.small:
Every time it happens, you go home angry.
You replay it all night.
Your family gets the guy who's still stuck in that meeting.

slides.big:
You don't have to be loud.
You just have to be on the record.
slides.small:
End each week with a 3-line email to your boss:
"Quick update: finished X, fixed Y, working on Z."
Facts. No bragging. Nobody can take credit for that.

slides.big:
Let the work speak.
But give it a microphone.
slides.small:
Save this for your next Friday.
